title: CacheGuardian: A Timing Side-Channel Resilient LLC Design
problem: The last-level cache (LLC) shared by multiple tenants in cloud computing is frequently exploited through timing side-channel attacks, enabling unauthorized data leakage. Existing defense mechanisms show deficiencies in performance overhead, attack coverage, and detection accuracy.
motivation: To provide stronger, broader, and more accurate protection against timing side-channel attacks with low performance overhead in shared LLC environments.
method: CacheGuardian protects the shared last-level cache using a hardware-based detector that monitors cache access patterns to identify various timing attacks in real time (attacks where someone measures how fast the cache responds to steal data). When it detects an attack, the system blocks only that attacker's access to specific cache sections rather than disrupting other users. This cache-set-level access control achieves fine-grained protection with minimal performance impact. The design was implemented and evaluated in gem5, a processor simulator.
key_novelty: CacheGuardian detects timing attacks by monitoring cache access patterns and blocks only the attacker's access to specific cache sections, enabling low-overhead protection.
contributions: Generic behavior-based attack detector capable of identifying multiple timing side-channel attacks in real time
Cache-set-level access control restricting cache usage to identified attackers
Up to 256× reduction in attack success rates including camouflaged variants
2.26% average performance improvement for benign workloads with only 2.4% storage overhead
limitations: The evaluation covers a range of timing attacks but may not address all possible variants or novel attack vectors.
